comments.body:
caused_by established — the cause site IS the fix site (date test applied).

`git log -S 'subprocess.Popen' -- src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py` returns exactly one
commit: 9f1e92c659 (2026-06-18, "feat(workflow): WS-D2 — hardened git-ref filesystem
snapshot"), the commit that created the file. The unbounded Popen, the undrained
`stderr=PIPE`, and the inherited stdin were all present from the first line of the file;
no later edit introduced or aggravated them (the only subsequent touches are
7622149b15/06e5992644/fc792e4f3c/997ecaabbf/a9aed66ce4 — prior-art hardening, ruff style,
the portable rename-then-chmod publish, and the BLE001/RUF ratchets).

Date test against the obligations that WOULD have caught it — every one of them POSTDATES
the cause commit, so this is NOT an unmet obligation of any of them:

  * 747f (blobless fetch, `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`)   — 2026-07-31
  * 77e1 (bound remaining network git calls)      — 2026-07-31
  * 12e4 (throughput-keyed stall abort)           — 2026-08-02
  * d37e (`check_raw_git_writes.py` marker gate)  — 2026-08-03
  * cause commit 9f1e92c659                       — 2026-06-18

The one precedent that predates it is c16f (5752edaefe, 2026-06-15, "bound network git
subprocesses with a timeout" on `_store/push.py`), three days earlier — but c16f scoped
itself to NETWORK git subprocesses, and `git archive` on a local repo only reaches the
network through the non-obvious promisor lazy-fetch path. Calling this an unmet c16f
obligation would be a stretch; the honest attribution is that WS-D2 (`humid-hub-sword`,
cf7c-1832-d5cd-4aa3) introduced the defect in the code it wrote. Linked caused_by.

Noting for completeness that 77e1's own commit message claims to "close the rest of the
class in the two modules that were still unbounded" (gerrit_client, opcert workspace) —
it missed this site because `git archive` was not classified as network-capable. That is a
classification gap in a sweep, not the origin of the defect.

RED -> GREEN and the mutation check.

RED (pre-fix), all for the stated reason:
  * stderr-flood      — driver child never returned; killed at the 90s hard bound. This is
                        the ticket's Repro B reproduced by the test itself.
  * stall             — same, at the 90s hard bound.
  * devnull/stall-args— KeyError: 'stdin' (no stdin kwarg was passed at all).
  * cred-redaction    — AttributeError: no `_redact_cmd`; TimeoutExpired had no conversion.
  * _GIT_TIMEOUT      — AssertionError: "snapshot.py declares no _GIT_TIMEOUT".

GREEN: 6/6 in 5.4s (the two that previously never returned now finish in well under a
second of archive time), 24/24 across the three snapshot test files, 737/737 in
tests/unit/workflow, 485 passed / 7 skipped across `-k "snapshot or raw_git or
module_size or timeout"`.

Mutation check — each defect re-seeded one at a time, confirming the matching test goes
back to RED and only that test:
  M1  drain thread target replaced with a no-op  -> stderr-flood FAILS at the 90s bound,
                                                    other 5 pass. KILLED.
  M2  `watchdog.start()` removed                 -> stall FAILS at the 90s bound,
                                                    other 5 pass. KILLED.
  M3  `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` removed         -> devnull test FAILS (KeyError 'stdin').
                                                    KILLED.
  M4  `*stall_abort_args()` removed from argv    -> same test FAILS on the argv assert.
                                                    KILLED.
  M5b `_redact_cmd(exc.cmd)` -> bare `exc.cmd`   -> cred test FAILS: the message rendered
                                                    "['git','fetch','https://bot:s3cr3t-
                                                    bot-token@...']" verbatim. KILLED.
  M6  `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` widened to `except (subprocess.SubprocessError,)`
      -> survives. Equivalent mutant by construction (TimeoutExpired's own base class);
      recorded rather than chased.

The credential-redaction test asked for by AC4 exists and is pinned twice: end-to-end
(`test_timeout_expired_cannot_leak_a_credential_url` drives the real `snapshot_at_ref`
against a Popen stand-in whose `wait` raises the 77e1-shaped TimeoutExpired, and asserts
neither the token nor the username survives into `str(SnapshotError)`) and at the unit
(`test_redactor_masks_url_userinfo_in_any_shape`, for both list and string `cmd` forms).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patch set 1 drew LLM-Review -1. One blocking finding plus three advisories; all four addressed in patch set 2.

BLOCKING (bugfix-size-attestation): 188 non-test lines is over the 150-line floor for a bug fix, and 093a carried no plan-review attestation. Earned one rather than gutting the change: `rebar review-plan gentile-armourclad-herring` returned verdict PASS, blocking=0, signed=true, and `--status` now reports verdict=certified (verified_at_sha c9a5388a838bc7a9933169ba540a27820c17151f, currency_basis file_impact). Four advisories came back on the plan itself — all about the description not COMMITTING to a fix mechanism (wall clock vs stall_abort_args vs both, and how stderr gets drained). All four were deferred by triage, and the shipped code in fact does exactly what they asked for: the stall abort is the primary instrument, the wall clock is an explicit backstop, and stderr is drained on its own thread. Leaving the description alone per the no-description-edits rule; recording the reconciliation here instead.

ADVISORIES, all three legitimate and all three fixed with a test each:
1. (error-handling) A Popen launch failure (git absent from PATH) is raised BEFORE the try/finally, so it escaped as a raw OSError and broke the module's documented 'raises SnapshotError on any failure' contract. Now wrapped. Test: test_launch_failure_is_a_snapshot_error_not_a_raw_oserror.
2. (security) The non-timeout failure branch interpolated the child's RAW stderr into the SnapshotError. A transport failure on the promisor lazy-fetch path echoes the promisor URL, which can carry credentials — the same leak class as TimeoutExpired.cmd, through a different door. The stderr now goes through _redact_cmd too.
3. (regression) The failure message had lost the sha context the pre-fix code carried ('git archive <sha[:12]> failed: ...'). Restored on all three failure branches.

Findings 2 and 3 are both pinned by test_failure_messages_name_the_sha_and_redact_child_stderr. Mutation-checked: M7 (drop the stderr redaction) FAILS on the leaked token, M8 (drop the OSError wrap) FAILS, M9 (drop the sha context) FAILS. Gates re-run clean: lint 0, typecheck 0, complexity active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0, raw-git-writes 0, 739/739 tests/unit/workflow.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patch set 2 CI failed — two repo-wide oracles I had not run locally (I had scoped to tests/unit/workflow). Both are real, both are mine, both fixed for patch set 3:

1. scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py — 'assert elapsed < _HARD_BOUND_SECONDS / 2' is an unescaped upper-bound wall-clock assert, the proven CI flake class (bugs 19d7, 5e94, edfe, 85c3). The assert is genuinely a stuck-run guard here (the pre-fix child stalls forever, so any finite ceiling separates fixed from broken, and 45s dwarfs the ~3s archive bound the test arms), so it takes the sanctioned inline escape: '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' on the line DIRECTLY above. Two lines above does not count; the gate re-fired until the marker moved.

2. tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py — the driver passed a plain 'dict(os.environ)' as env=, which pytest's long traceback would print in full on a spawn failure. Switched to tests/_subprocess_env.subprocess_env(), the representation-safe boundary whose repr redacts the values.

Process note for the next agent on this file: 'make lint' + 'make typecheck' + the complexity ratchet are NOT the whole gate. The build also runs check_comment_hygiene, check_raw_git_writes, check_server_manifest, check_verify_gate_parity and check_wall_clock_asserts as separate steps, and repo-wide pytest oracles (the subprocess-env one above) can fail on a file you only exercised through its own directory. All five gate scripts now pass locally and the full tests/unit sweep is running before the re-push.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`llm/workflow/snapshot.py:181-187` streams `git archive` through a pipe with **no timeout, an
undrained stderr pipe, and inherited stdin**:

```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["git", "-C", root, "archive", "--format=tar", sha],
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,          # never drained until AFTER the tar stream
)
with tarfile.open(fileobj=proc.stdout, mode="r|") as tar:   # :187 — blocks here
    tar.extractall(path=str(tmp), filter=_hardened_filter(max_bytes))
_, stderr = proc.communicate()        # unreachable while :187 blocks; also unbounded
```

Three defects in one call:

1. **No `timeout=`** on the `Popen` or on `communicate()`.
2. **`stderr=PIPE` is never drained** while stdout is being consumed. If the child writes more
   than the pipe buffer (~64 KiB) to stderr, it blocks writing stderr, therefore stops writing
   stdout, and the parent blocks forever in `tarfile.__read` waiting for stdout. Classic
   undrained-pipe deadlock; needs no network and no partial clone.
3. **stdin is inherited** (no `stdin=DEVNULL`), unlike `_store/push.py:221` and
   `enrich_drain.py:329` which do set it — so a credential or host-key prompt can block here too.

## Reproduced deterministically (twice)

Found while investigating `unquieting-godsent-mammal` (`b405-d5ec-30b3-4538`). Both reproductions
drove the REAL `snapshot_at_ref` and blocked at the same line, with byte-identical stacks:

```
File ".../tarfile.py", line 566 in __read
...
File ".../src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py", line 187 in snapshot_at_ref
```

**Repro A — promisor lazy-fetch stall.** A partial clone (`--filter=blob:none`) with 4 genuinely
missing blobs, its promisor remote repointed at a TCP black hole (accepts, never replies). The
process sat at `STAT=SN, %CPU 0.0` for 4m26s with zero bytes on stdout and stderr, and was still
blocked when killed. `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT=5` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` were both set and neither
rescued it. A **control on a full (non-partial) clone against the same black hole completed in
0.02 s**, proving the stall is reached only through the lazy-fetch path.

**Repro B — stderr deadlock, no network at all.** A fake `git` on `PATH` writing a valid tar to
stdout and ~200 KB to stderr midway, against a healthy local clone. Parent and child both wedged
at `SN / 0.0%` indefinitely.

## Honest scope: this is NOT the cause of b405

`snapshot_at_ref` is referenced only at `llm/workflow/__init__.py:66` (an export) and is **not
reachable from `llm/plan_review/` or `_commands/close_precheck.py`** — verified by grep over
`src/rebar`. So it is not on the `review-plan` / `transition -> closed` paths that hang in the
field. Filing it separately rather than folding it into b405, because attaching a real-but-
off-path finding to that investigation would corrupt its evidence.

Note also that repro B's trigger has not been shown to occur naturally: a real `git archive`
emitted **0 bytes** of stderr in measurement, because git suppresses progress when stderr is not a
TTY — and `Popen` gives it a pipe. So defect 2 is a **proven latent deadlock**, not an observed
field failure. Defect 1 (the promisor stall) is the one with a demonstrated multi-minute block.

## Constraints on the fix (from prior tickets)

- `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` is neither `OSError` nor `CalledProcessError`, so it escapes existing
  `except` tuples, and `TimeoutExpired.cmd` carries any `user:token@host` URL — found the hard way
  in `dominant-northbound-blackrhino` (`77e1-7f82-98e6-4fed`). Route it through this module's
  error conversion or a hang becomes a credential disclosure.
- Elapsed time is the wrong axis for a stalled transfer (`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:169`);
  `suave-constant-cow` (`12e4-8c74-a738-4014`) built the reusable `stall_abort_args()` seam
  (`http.lowSpeedLimit` / `lowSpeedTime`). Prefer splicing that for any network-reaching git call
  over only shortening a wall clock.
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` requires a `# raw-git-ok:` marker on new/edited raw git
  subprocess sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `git archive` child that writes more than the pipe buffer to stderr does not deadlock the
      parent — verified by a test using a fake `git` that does exactly that, observed FAILING
      before the fix.
- [ ] The subprocess is bounded, and a stalled child is terminated rather than left running —
      verified by a test that stalls the child and asserts both that the call returns and that no
      orphan child survives.
- [ ] `stdin` is not inherited, so no prompt can block this call.
- [ ] A `TimeoutExpired` raised here cannot leak a credential-bearing command line into an error
      message or log — verified by a test asserting the redaction.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

file_impact.reason: Popen git archive at :181 has no timeout, leaves stderr=PIPE undrained while consuming stdout, and inherits stdin; blocks at :187.
New tests: stderr-flood deadlock, stalled-child bounding and orphan reaping, credential redaction on TimeoutExpired.
